note: Shore zones (docs/future/10, src/world/water/shore.js): the shore banded by how long each height spends under the sea, as on real rocky and sandy shores. Each zone names the painted ground it shows on (the most painted of grass, sand, rock and soil in each 0.5 m cell) and its height range in A0, the base tide amplitude (water.json tide.amplitudeM): the tide band runs from -bandFactor to +bandFactor A0 (spring low to spring high), and the splash ground above it to +bandFactor + splashFactor A0 (water.json summary). Neap tides turn at +-(1 - springNeap) A0. A cell takes the first zone in the list that matches; ground with no zone (grass, or a height no zone covers) shows nothing new. Kelp sits below the neap low, so it only shows at spring low tides. cover: how much of each look the zone carries, 0..1 (wrack: seaweed over the rock; kelp: kelp blades over the rock; ripples: wave ripples in the sand; lichen: black crust on splash rock; mud: soft, wet, dark soil). taper: how much the cover thins from the zone's bottom to its top (0 none, 1 gone at the top), so a zone has no hard upper edge. These go to the shore texture (src/world/water/shore-live.js) the terrain reads.

lookNote: The look of the zones (Z2), physical and linear like every material: albedo values are linear reflectance. Wrack is drawn on the moss scan's layer (it never grows in the tide band, so the two never meet) with its own albedo: the scan is rescaled from terrain.json materials.albedoMoss to wrackAlbedo, until a wrack scan of its own is chosen. clumpM: sizes (m) of the clumps wrack and lichen grow in. Ripples are drawn, not scanned: crests run along the shore, wavelengthM apart, leaning by slope; they fade out as a pixel grows from a fourteenth to a sixth of a wavelength, so far views never show contour lines, and are off on the tiers listed in offTiers. Lichen multiplies the rock's albedo by lichenAlbedo where it grows. Mud darkens soil by mudAlbedo and holds it at mudWet wetness, so it shines.

look.kelpNote: Kelp (Laminaria) is drawn, not scanned (no CC0 seaweed scan exists): broad, glossy, dark olive blades lying downslope over rock in the kelp zone, tapering to tip and base, with a raised midrib, overlapping. widthM: a blade's widest half-width; cellM: the grid across and along the slope that places one blade per cell; lengthM: blade length range; relief: how much the midrib lifts the light; albedo: wet kelp, linear.
look.frondsNote: Wrack fronds (bladderwrack) are drawn close up over the wrack mat (lib-shore wrackFronds): narrow straps draped downslope, forking once and often twice, with paired air bladders either side of the midrib. widthM: a strap's half-width; cellM: the grid across and along the slope, one frond per cell; lengthM: frond length range; bladderM: a bladder's radius; relief: how much midrib and bladders lift the light; albedo: wet wrack, linear; bladderTone: bladders' albedo as a share of the fronds' (lighter, yellower); fadeM: view distances over which fronds give way to the mat; hideMat: how much of the mat the fronds hide close up; offTiers: tiers that keep the mat only.
look.strandlineNote: The strandline (src/world/water/strandline.js): each of the last lookbackTides high waters leaves a line of litter at its level plus runupM (the waves run up), unless a later high water reached higher and swept it up; at most maxLines lie at once, the newest first, each fading over fadeHours as it dries and scatters. halfWidthM: how far (m, across the shore) the litter spreads either side of the line, varied by slow noise. density: the most strands present on a fresh line. strand: thin pieces of dried wrack, cellM grid, lengthM range, widthM half-width, crossShare lying crossways, albedo dried litter (linear). kelpShare: how many broken kelp blades lie in the line. offTiers: tiers that draw the line as a tint without strands.
